questions.stem: A dispatch service picks a courier with `couriers.parallelStream().filter(Courier::isFree).findAny()`. The list holds 40 couriers sorted by distance, nearest first, and the 2nd, 9th, 15th and 30th are free. Which courier does it pick?

options.text: The 2nd, since findAny returns the first match in the list's order
options.says: returning the first match in encounter order is findFirst's promise; findAny is explicitly nondeterministic

options.text: The 2nd, since a parallel stream searches the nearest couriers first
options.says: the chunks are searched at the same time, and findAny takes a match from whichever chunk finds one

options.text: One of the four, differing between runs, since findAny returns whichever match a worker thread reaches
options.says: findAny is free to return any match; on a parallel stream it varies from run to run

options.text: One of the four, differing between runs, since a parallel stream gives every terminal operation its matches in no order
options.says: findFirst on the same parallel stream would always return the 2nd; only findAny gives up the order

origin.section: findAny Is Free to Return Any Match

questions.stem: A monitoring job reports the slowest response of the last minute with `latencies.stream().reduce(Long.MIN_VALUE, Math::max)`, where `latencies` is a `List<Long>`. In a minute with no requests, the list is empty. What does the job report?

options.text: It reports -9223372036854775808, since an empty reduce hands back the value it was told to start from
options.says: an empty stream returns the identity, and nothing downstream can tell it from a real latency

options.text: It reports 0, since an empty reduce hands back the default value of its element type
options.says: reduce knows nothing of zero; with an identity, the empty result is the identity

options.text: It throws NoSuchElementException, since an empty reduce has nothing to compare with Long.MIN_VALUE
options.says: reduce with an identity never throws for an empty stream; it returns the identity

options.text: It returns Optional.empty(), since an empty reduce has nothing to compare with Long.MIN_VALUE
options.says: only reduce without an identity returns an Optional; this form returns a Long

origin.section: Without an Identity, reduce Returns an Optional, and So Do min, max and findFirst

questions.stem: A text service counts the words longer than ten characters with `words.reduce(0, (n, w) -> w.length() > 10 ? n + 1 : n, (a, b) -> a + 1)`. Its unit tests pass sequential streams and give the right counts. What happens when production passes a large parallel stream?

options.text: Right counts, since only the accumulator's n + 1 counts and (a, b) -> a + 1 just joins chunks
options.says: the third function, the combiner, merges partial counts, and adding 1 instead of b throws away each right-hand chunk's count

options.text: Right counts, since the sequential tests already ran (a, b) -> a + 1 on every merge of two counts
options.says: a sequential stream never calls the combiner, so the tests never ran it

options.text: Wrong counts, since the sequential tests never ran (a, b) -> a + 1, which drops the count in b
options.says: the combiner must agree with the accumulator: merging a partial count must add it, and only a parallel run calls the combiner

options.text: Wrong counts, since the accumulator's n + 1 runs on several threads at once and loses updates
options.says: each chunk folds into its own partial result, so the accumulator shares nothing between threads

origin.section: The Three-Argument Form's Combiner Runs Only on a Parallel Stream

questions.stem: An audit log writes `"tags: " + tags.stream().collect(Collectors.joining("; ", "<", ">"))` for every record. What does it write for a record whose `tags` list is empty?

options.text: `tags: <>`, since joining writes its prefix and suffix around an empty stream too
options.says: joining with a prefix and suffix gives prefix + suffix for an empty stream

options.text: `tags: <;>`, since joining writes one delimiter between its prefix and suffix around an empty stream
options.says: the delimiter goes only between two elements, and an empty stream has none

options.text: `tags: `, since joining leaves out its prefix and suffix around an empty stream
options.says: the prefix and suffix are written even for an empty stream

options.text: `tags: null`, since joining returns null instead of a string for an empty stream
options.says: joining always returns a String; for an empty stream it is prefix + suffix

origin.section: teeing Feeds Two Collectors in One Pass, and joining Writes Its Prefix Even for Nothing
